_comment: Tunables for the leaked-source forensics layers of analyze_artifact.py: tools/bp_archive_time.py (member-source reader + timestamp forensics), tools/bp_git.py (embedded .git + module identifiers) and tools/bp_keys.py (SPKI key dedupe). Everything these layers report is a FACT or a LEAD (rung 'lead') — a committer string, a module path, a packer timezone or a shared key is never a KB edge and never names an operator on its own. Extend the lists here, not in Python.

source_limits._comment: Caps on what one run reads from an archive or directory. max_members = members enumerated (the rest are counted, not read); max_member_bytes = bytes read from any single member; max_total_bytes = read budget across all layers sharing one source; max_walk_depth = directory recursion depth for a local directory target.

archive_time._comment: Bulk-copy cluster = one second (zip: DOS 2-second granularity) shared by >= bulk_min_files files OR by >= bulk_min_fraction of all files (and at least bulk_floor files). seq_* = sequential generation run: >= seq_min_files files whose consecutive mtimes are <= seq_max_gap_seconds apart and span >= 2 distinct seconds. implausible_before_year = earliest year accepted as a real authoring time (DOS 1980-01-01 and tar epoch 0 are counted as stripped, not implausible). future_slack_seconds = tolerance past 'now' before a date is called future. max_events = rows kept in events[]. offset_round_minutes = rounding for the DOS-local vs UT/NTFS-UTC packer offset.

author_path_patterns._comment: Regexes (Python, case-insensitive) whose FIRST group is a username / hostname leaked in a member path or a small text member. A hit says the packer's environment leaked; it is a lead, never an identity on its own.

author_ignore_users._comment: Path usernames that are build-system or placeholder accounts, not people (CI runners, container defaults, documentation placeholders).

git._comment: max_objects = loose objects inspected per repo; max_commits = commit rows kept in commits[]; max_pack_bytes = largest packfile walked for commit/tag objects (bigger packs are listed and counted only); max_object_bytes = largest single decompressed commit/tag object kept; max_reflog_lines per repo; max_identities kept.

module_files._comment: Manifest file basename -> ecosystem. Their declared module path / package name / author / repository survive re-skinning of the product and are leads to the original project.

module_skip_dirs._comment: Path components whose manifests are third-party dependencies, not the leaked project itself.

keys._comment: max_scan_bytes = largest member scanned for key material; max_keys = distinct keys kept; max_occurrences = occurrences kept per key. text_extensions are scanned even if they look binary; der_extensions are tried as raw DER; keystore_extensions are recorded as present-but-opaque (password-protected containers).

key_der_extensions._comment: Member extensions tried as raw DER (certificate / SPKI / PKCS#1 / PKCS#8 / SEC1).

key_keystore_extensions._comment: Password-protected key containers: recorded with spki_sha256=null and a reason (opening them needs the password and a crypto library).

benign_spki_sha256._comment: SHA-256 (hex, lower-case) of SubjectPublicKeyInfo DER for PUBLIC demo / test / documentation keys that ship in many unrelated projects (framework sample keys, library test vectors). A match is marked benign: it links nothing. Seeded with one synthetic sentinel (64 zeros) that no real SPKI hashes to, because reference value lists must be non-empty; add a real hash only after confirming the key is published as a sample.
